Whole exome sequencing, explained

A short, plain-language look at what whole exome sequencing is and how it works.

What WES analyzes

The 1% of the genome that carries most of the answers

The exome is only about 1–2% of your DNA, but it holds the large majority of the genetic changes we currently know how to link to health conditions. Instead of testing one gene at a time — which can stretch a diagnosis over many months — Xenome WES looks at all ~20,000 of these genes at once, in a single test. That means clearer answers can arrive sooner, from one simple swab of the cheek.

What it can mean for you

Why families choose Xenome

  • An answer, sooner. One test can replace years of separate work-ups and waiting for the next appointment.
  • Guidance you can act on. A clear diagnosis can shape treatment, follow-up, and medication decisions with your care team.
  • Understanding for your family. Results can help explain what a condition may mean for relatives and future children.
  • It works alongside your care. Genetic answers add to — they don't replace — the care and support you already receive.
Who this test can help Xenome WES is offered for patients with a primary diagnosis of Autism or Epilepsy.
